attributes.title: Level 1

subgroups.name: build 1

steps.hints: ❓ Did you rename the 6 image assets from the in My Assets?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ How is adding an image to My Assets similar and different to how you’ve previously added sprite images?

❓ Why might it be useful to add an image to My Assets?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Explain to the ninja the benefits of using the Assets menu. In the JavaScript editor, it can be very helpful to use the Assets menu to save images, tiles, tilemaps, and animations because the JavaScript editor has fewer visual supports as compared to the blocks editor. As a result, typing out the name of an asset is easier than copying the code or searching for a specific image in the Gallery. 

💡 Point out to the ninja what happens when they select a specific asset. On the left side menu, a preview of the asset appears and tells about its properties (type and size). From this side menu, the asset can be edited, duplicated, copied, or deleted.
steps.instructions:
Begin the project by naming 6 different item images in My Assets to be placed on a bookcase.


Click the Assets menu along the top of the screen, and notice there's a bookcase image, as well as 6 additional image assets in My Assets. Each image asset can be edited, duplicated, copied, or deleted by selecting it. Select an image, then click Edit to open it.


Notice the white box on the bottom of the screen with the name of the image. Replace “myImage'' with a descriptive name that will be used in the project code. Click Done to add the image to My Assets. 


Repeat this process to create 5 additional item image assets for the bookcase. Rename each image before clicking Done.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you create an original tile asset that can be used as a shelf, like this?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ Where will the shelf tile appear in the tilemap editor?

❓ How can you edit a tile asset once it has been created?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Point out to the ninja that they give their tile a descriptive name and use camelCase in the title.

💡 Remind the ninja that any custom tile will appear in the My Tiles category of the tilemap editor. This will be useful for adding the shelf tile onto the tilemap.

💡 Point out to the ninja what happens when they select a specific asset. On the left side menu, a preview of the asset appears and tells about its properties (type and size). From this side menu, the asset can be edited, duplicated, copied, or deleted. Additionally, a tile icon will appear on the bottom left corner of any tile asset in My Assets.
steps.instructions:
Create an original tile in My Assets! 

Click the green (+) to add a new asset to My Assets. From the Create New Asset menu, select Tile.


Using the editor tools, design a tile to be used as a simple shelf for item sprites to appear on top of. Replace “myTile” with a descriptive name that will be used in the project code. Click Done to add the tile to My Assets.


Notice how the tile appears in My Assets and can be edited, duplicated, copied, or deleted by selecting it.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you resize the tilemap to 10 x 8 ?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What size should the tilemap be? How can the dimensions be updated?

❓ What other tools are available in the tilemap editor?

❓ Where might the shelf tiles be added to create a tilemap that looks like a bookcase?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Remind the ninja of the different features of the tilemap editor. When editing a tilemap, the ninja has all of the same paint tools available to them. However, they can also enable walls and select tiles to “paint” with. Point out that the tilemap dimensions can be updated in the bottom left corner of the editor.

💡 Remind the ninja that any custom tile will appear in the My Tiles tab of the tilemap editor. This will be useful for adding the shelf tile onto the tilemap.

💡 Point out to the ninja what happens when they select a specific asset. On the left side menu, a preview of the asset appears and tells about its properties (type and size). From this side menu, the asset can be edited, duplicated, copied, or deleted.
steps.instructions:
Place the shelves on the bookcase by creating a tilemap in My Assets! 


Click ▶ and notice there is already a background image of a bookcase on the screen. Use a tilemap to create the shelves to place the items on. A tilemap is made up of 16 x 16 pixel square tiles that create a layout or map for a project.


Click the green (+) again. From the Create New Asset menu, select Tilemap. 


Resize the tilemap to 10 x 8 by changing the numbers on the bottom left of the editor. 


Click on My Tiles, then select the tile created in the previous step. Use the new tile to design a tilemap of shelf tiles that will appear in the center of the bookcase. Replace “level” with a descriptive name, such as “tilemap1.” Click Done to add the tilemap to My Assets.


Notice how the tilemap appears in My Assets and can be edited, duplicated, copied, or deleted by selecting it.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you use // to add comments to better organize your code?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What code might be placed underneath each comment?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Remind the ninja that typing // tells the project to skip over the text that follows and move onto the next line of code. Just as when naming assets, it’s useful to be short and descriptive when writing comments.
steps.instructions:
Add code comments to organize where the code will go in the editor!


Click the JavaScript tab at the top of the screen to return to the coding editor. Then, add comments for tilemap set up and sprite set up.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you type assets and a dot operator, select tilemap from the code completion tool, then type the name of the tilemap asset inside 2 backticks `` in the tilemap parameter?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ How is setting a tilemap in the JavaScript editor similar and different to doing so in the blocks editor? 

❓ How can you check the name of the tilemap stored in My Assets?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 In the blocks editor, there was a gray box that showed a preview of the tilemap and could be selected to edit the tilemap. In the JavaScript editor, it is easier to save the tilemap as an asset, then call the asset in a line of code. Encourage the ninja to double check that they have placed the asset type and asset name correctly in their code.

💡 If the ninja forgot the name of their tilemap asset, they should click over to the Assets menu, then select the tilemap to see the preview with the asset name on the left side.
steps.instructions:
Set the shelf tilemap to appear on top of the background image!


Open Scene and drag [set tilemap to (tilemap)] under the setBackgroundImage code. Notice how the code block turns into JavaScript text: 

tiles.setCurrentTilemap(tilemap``)

The setCurrentTilemap function takes 1 parameter: tilemap. To access the tilemap created in My Assets, type assets followed by a dot operator before tilemap`` inside the parentheses. Then type the name given to the tilemap inside the 2 backticks ``. 


Click ▶ to see the shelf tilemap appear on top of the background image.


Click the tilemap icon to the left of the line of code to make any changes to the tilemap.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you type assets and a dot operator, select image from the code completion tool, then type the name of the image asset inside 2 backticks `` in the image parameter?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ How is using an asset to set a sprite’s image similar and different to how you’ve done so before?

❓ How can you check the name of an image stored in My Assets?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Point out to the ninja that they have previously saved images as variables, then used the variable name to refer to those images in their project code. Using an image stored in My Assets is very similar—the image is stored in a separate location and is called in a specific line of code in the project. Have the ninja notice how much shorter the image asset code is, as opposed to when img`` is used. Encourage the ninja to double check that they have placed the asset type and asset name correctly in their code.

💡 If the ninja forgot the name of their image asset, they should click over to the Assets menu, then select each image to see the preview with the asset name on the left side.

💡 Encourage the ninja to use documentation if they need assistance adding 6 new sprites to the project. Because sprites will not interact with one another in this project, sprite kinds are not necessary to include.
steps.instructions:
Display the 6 sprite image assets from My Assets on screen!


Add code to create 6 sprites in the project underneath // sprite set up.


Name each sprite to match the name of the asset created in My Assets, then replace img`...` by typing assets, a dot operator, and image. Type the name given to the sprite’s image asset surrounded by 2 backticks ` `.


Click ▶ to see the item sprites appear on the screen.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you notice that tilemap coordinates begin at 0 and increase from left to right (column) and top to bottom (row)?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ How is placing a sprite on a tilemap in the JavaScript editor similar and different to doing so in the blocks editor? 

❓ Where can you find the coordinates of a specific tile in the tilemap editor?


Sensei Pro Tip: 

💡 In the blocks editor, the [place (sprite) on top of tilemap (col) (row)] block had inputs for the sprite, column, and row coordinates. Prompt the ninja to notice that in the JavaScript editor, the getTileLocation function is used to find the column and row coordinates of a tile on the tilemap. 

💡 Remind the ninja that tilemaps use columns and rows to determine the location of specific tiles. Explain that coordinates begin at 0 and increase from left to right (column) and top to bottom (row). The ninja can use their cursor to hover over a specific tile, then find its coordinates in the bottom left corner of the tilemap editor.
steps.instructions:
Place the item sprites on shelf tiles.


Open Scene and drag [place (mySprite) on top of (loc)] under the code that sets one of the item sprites. Notice how the code block turns into JavaScript text: 

tiles.placeOnTile(mySprite, tiles.getTileLocation(0, 0))


The placeOnTile function takes 2 parameters: sprite and location. Replace mySprite with the sprite name. Update the tilemap coordinates in the location parameter to place the item sprite on a specific shelf tile on the tilemap. 


Repeat the process to place the other 5 sprites on the shelf tiles.


Click ▶ to see the 6 items appear on the shelves!
